commits.message: fix(color): the surface a translucent background composites over is the caller's — black for the terminal writer, the canvas for an export
test(color): the truecolor path is pinned on a background translucency visibly changes
fix(color): contrast is chosen against a translucent background as the writer draws it

feat(color): text floors hold at 256 colours; downgrades never pick ANSI 0-15 (#155)

* feat(color): text keeps its contrast at 256 colours; downgrades never pick terminal-defined ANSI 0-15

A downgrade to 256 colours matched against all 256 entries, so it could land
on ANSI 0-15, whose RGB every terminal theme redefines, and Style.toSgrCodes
rounded text and background independently, so two roundings could meet in
the middle: a 4.57:1 pair drew at 3.25:1.

- EIGHT_BIT_DOWNGRADE_TABLE holds the cube and grey ramp (16-255); ColorTable
  takes a firstIndex so its matches are terminal indices.
- ColorTable.matchReadable: the nearest entry that clears a ratio against a
  background, else the most contrast.
- ColorSpec.downgradeOn(target, bg): at 256 colours text keeps the contrast
  the truecolor pair had (or the most the palette offers on the drawn bg);
  elsewhere the drawn RGB is the terminal's and text downgrades alone.
- relativeLuminance/contrastRatio move to core/color.ts, below both the
  theme math and the SGR writer; themes/colorMath re-exports them.

* fix(color): measure the floor where text is chosen, not in the SGR writer

Review of #155: downgradeOn treated every foreground as text, so powerline
arrows (fg = a neighbour's bg) and gradient half-blocks were dragged to grey,
and an exact-ratio target recoloured text still legible after plain rounding.
At the writer a text foreground and a fill foreground are the same value, so
the rule moves to the choice: ensureContrast(fg, bg, ratio, drawnAt) measures
on the pair the terminal draws and, at 256, falls back to the nearest
cube/grey entry that clears the floor (which rounds to itself). The writer
rounds every colour on its own again, as Python Rich does.

- remove ColorSpec.downgradeOn; toSgrCodes is master's again
- ensureContrast gains drawnAt (default TRUECOLOR); ansi/default unmeasurable
- colorFuncs/richTextFuncs take a drawnAt getter; readableOnFunc exported
- ColorTable caches entry luminances; size documented as an entry count

* docs(examples): demonstrate readableOnFunc at 256 colours

* docs(examples): one 256-colour engine; readableOn demos pass the required ratio

* fix(color): ColorTable memos are bounded — a long-running host no longer grows them per colour

* chore(release): 0.13.0

* fix(template-bindings): drawnAt documented and defaulted once; binding pinned through an engine

* docs: richTextFuncs' drawnAt, readableOnFunc, and the 16-255 downgrade table

* fix(color): one WCAG ratio formula; matchReadable pinned directly; contrast docs name drawnAt

* docs(contrast): the 256-colour path's fallback when no entry clears the ratio

* docs(template-bindings): point to contrast.md for the drawn-depth guarantee
